qt: to the Commission Kostas Papadakis (NI) Subject:

According to official statements made by the leadership of the Greek Ministry of Rural Development and Food and of the Directorate-General for Veterinary Affairs before a committee of the Greek Parliament, the government claims, on the one hand, that sufficient quantities of approved foot-and-mouth vaccines are not available and, on the other, that the European Union has called for serological testing for pox on samples from sheep and goat herds. The Ministry of Rural Development and Food has highlighted that any herds testing positive in these serological checks will be mandatorily culled in their entireties. At the same time, public allegations regarding the scale of illegal vaccinations – with talk of over a million animals – were also made by the then minister and the then head of the scientific committee for the control of pox. This situation is the direct result of the criminal understaffing of state veterinary services, the lack of effective prevention measures and the refusal to implement a state-run, organised free vaccination programme. With this in mind, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What view does it take of the fact that the EU regulatory framework mandates the culling of herds testing positive for pox in serological checks, rather than promoting an evidence-based, state-run free vaccination programme?

What view does it take on the Greek Government’s claims that there are serious shortages in the availability of the necessary vaccines for foot-and-mouth disease, and what measures is it taking to secure them immediately through the European vaccine bank?
What immediate measures does it intend to take to ensure that struggling livestock farmers do not pay the price for the selective inability of the Greek state and the EU to control animal diseases?
